claims.claim: on an untrapped site in south-central Maine beaver colonies rose from 0.15 to 0.32 per km² in 1988–92 and open water by 36 %
claims.note: The abstract says the same (colonies 0.15 to 0.32/km², +113 %, on a 111-km² site closed to trapping; surface water 115 to 158 ha, +36 %), but the full text was not read.

claims.claim: breeding hooded mergansers rose to 23–29 per 100 km² on an untrapped south-central Maine site as beaver wetlands expanded
claims.note: The abstract lists hooded mergansers '(23-29/100 km2)' among species that increased, which reads as a rise FROM 23 TO 29 per 100 km², and the study measured densities of breeding PAIRS. If the full text agrees, write 'breeding pairs rose from 23 to 29 per 100 km²'. The abstract also says more than 3–4 years may be needed for waterfowl densities to respond.

claims.claim: colonies rose from 0.15 to 0.32 per km² in 1988–92, open water by 36 %; wetland area tracked colony density (r = 0.99); a trapped site held 0.19–0.20 colonies per km²
claims.note: The abstract contradicts the r = 0.99 attribution: r = 0.99 (n = 4 years, P = 0.009) is between the NUMBER OF BEAVER DAMS maintained and colony density; the NUMBER OF WETLANDS correlated at r = 0.92 (n = 4, P = 0.081, not significant at 0.05); no correlation for wetland AREA is given. The research note (shore_birds_and_mammals.md) says 'dams and wetlands tracked colony density (r = 0.99)'; the paper turned that into wetland area. Trapped site 0.19–0.20/km² agrees with the abstract.
